source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting structural defects in a bridge maintenance report

1. Start with the maintenance records.
2.
completion:
Review and gather all past maintenance records of the bridge, including previous inspection reports, documented defects, repairs, and any relevant notes. This serves as a foundation for understanding the bridge's history and can provide insight into recurring issues.

3. Conduct a detailed inspection.
Organize a thorough inspection of the bridge, carefully following established safety protocols. Use checklists to ensure all aspects of the bridge are examined, including the superstructure (beams and girders), substructure (piers and abutments), deck (roadway surface), bearings, expansion joints, and any other unique features.

4. Document the location of defects.
Upon identifying any defects, precisely note their locations using a consistent reference system (e.g., GPS coordinates, distance from known landmarks, or grid/milestone markers). Include drawings or sketches that illustrate the location, orientation, and extent of damage.

5. Describe the nature of the defects.
Provide a detailed description of each defect,
